verdict.rationale: Kintsugi documents a broad REST API and five official SDKs. They cover transaction sync, tax estimates, credit notes, nexus listing, registration creation, filings retrieval, exemption creation and certificate upload, so much of the core compliance workflow is programmable. However, there is no stated UI/API parity, and some actions are described as app-only: API keys are created in the app, and data-source connectors are connected from the app's Data Sources screen. Missing for 10: an explicit UI/API parity commitment, API endpoints for key management and connector setup, and independent corroboration of coverage breadth.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can do everything through the API that I can do in the UI

citations.quote: Build against the REST API or an official SDK.
The Create Registration API allows users to create a new registration for tracking and managing tax filings efficiently across multiple jurisdictions.
The Get Filings API retrieves a paginated list of filings based on filters such as dates, jurisdiction, Country, status, etc.
The Upload Exemption Certificate API allows you to upload a file attachment (e.g., exemption certificate) for a specific exemption.
This page covers creating a key in the app, the one moment you can copy it, and how to manage keys after that.
